root_idea.summary: The root denotes a vehement sound or noise, especially one produced by forceful impact and capable of deafening.
root_idea.development: The lexical field extends from forceful striking and resounding noise to deafening cries, piercing action, and related figurative uses. In the Quranic noun, this sound-field is concentrated in the deafening eschatological cry or blast associated with the Resurrection.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Classical Arabic citation form صَاخَّةٌ rather than the inflected QAC surface form.

senses.definition: The deafening eschatological cry or blast.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic usage, it is the vehement sound associated with the Resurrection; one classical interpretation identifies it specifically as the second blast of the trumpet.

senses.definition: The Resurrection itself, used as a designation for the eschatological event.
senses.usage_conditions: In the interpretation of 80:33, the noun may designate the Resurrection rather than the cry or blast that announces or occasions it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To produce a sound so vehement that it deafens the ear; to strike someone on the ear and render him deaf.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence includes both a vehement sound as the cause and a direct strike upon the ear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To accuse someone of a grave crime and calumniate him.
To strike or cast something at someone so as to cause extreme pain; according to an attributed variant report, to kill him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported of a shot or cast directed at a person; the killing implication is presented as an alternative attribution in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pierce sharply with the beak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression of a crow piercing into the sore or gall on a camel’s back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Striking something hard against a solid object, including striking iron against iron.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal-noun usage concerning forceful impact and the resulting hard sound.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To produce a sound when struck, as a stone or mass of rock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a solid object whose sound is heard upon being struck.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To listen attentively to someone’s narration or discourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with لِـ in the cited construction صَخَّ لِحَدِيثِهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sound produced when a mass of rock is struck with a stone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete sound noun for the noise of rock striking rock.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A calamity or misfortune, especially a severe one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical Arabic use; the same lexical discussion relates the term’s designation of the Resurrection to its character as a severe calamity.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only cross-reference to the first sentence of another entry.
Covers the deafening cry or blast, including the second trumpet blast, and the interpretation of the term as the Resurrection.
Covers the broader sense of severe calamity and its application as a name for the Resurrection.

cautions: QAC classifies the Quranic occurrence as an active participle, while the Classical lexical discussion also records an infinitival interpretation.

The Quranic noun has two closely related traditional interpretations: the deafening eschatological cry or blast, and the Resurrection itself. No Lane citation has been converted from historical notation into an unsupported modern verse location.
